main_issue: Whether and where Agent D can chant at 4:45 a.m. daily without waking the other three, and who should bear the burden of changing

A-B.evidence: B echoes A's point that sound travels (T6) and backs moving outside (T16, T18); A proposed the void deck (T13).

A-C.evidence: Both say the chanting disrupts their sleep (T1, T7, T21, T23); C never speaks to A directly, though both oppose D's in-flat options.

A-D.evidence: A rejects D's quieter, whisper and living-room offers (T3, T9, T11) and suggests the void deck; D refuses it as unsafe (T14), saying only 'leave' has been suggested (T22).

B-C.evidence: Both say they cannot sleep through it and that it must change (T18, T21, T23); neither addresses the other.

B-D.evidence: B says quieter is not enough (T6) and asks for somewhere outside (T16); D replies 'why do I have to be the one to go outside?' (T17), and B restates the sleep need (T18).

C-D.evidence: C asks if the time can change (T19), D says no (T20); C says she won't be able to sleep (T21, T23), and D rejects leaving the flat as unfair (T22, T24).
